IAFahim.DS.Mo.readme:
# IAFahim.DS.Mo

## Use case
Curious cat uses Mo’s ordering to batch offline range queries. It reduces pointer movement so many queries can share work.

IAFahim.DS.OrderedSet.readme:
# IAFahim.DS.OrderedSet

## Use case
Curious cat uses an ordered set for sorted inserts, deletes, and rank queries. It helps when the cat wants both order and fast updates.

IAFahim.DS.SegmentTree.readme:
# IAFahim.DS.SegmentTree

## Use case
Curious cat uses a segment tree for fast range queries and updates. It is the cat’s choice for logs of min/max/sum over intervals.

IAFahim.DS.Sparse.readme:
# IAFahim.DS.Sparse

## Use case
Curious cat uses a sparse table when data is static and queries must be lightning fast. It precomputes overlaps for O(1) range answers.

IAFahim.DS.Splay.readme:
# IAFahim.DS.Splay

## Use case
Curious cat uses a splay tree when access patterns are skewed. It moves hot nodes to the top so repeated queries get faster.

IAFahim.DS.Treap.readme:
# IAFahim.DS.Treap

## Use case
Curious cat uses a treap for a randomized balanced BST without heavy rotations. It keeps ordered operations simple and reliable.

IAFahim.DS.Trie.readme:
# IAFahim.DS.Trie

## Use case
Curious cat uses a trie to store many strings by shared prefixes. It makes prefix checks and dictionary lookups swift.

IAFahim.DS.UnsafeArray.readme:
# IAFahim.DS.UnsafeArray

## Use case
Curious cat uses UnsafeArray when it wants raw, unmanaged storage it can free itself. It fits low‑level algorithms that must own memory.

IAFahim.GameTheory.readme:
# IAFahim.GameTheory

## Use case
Curious cat uses game theory algorithms to decide winning and losing positions. It helps the cat compute optimal moves in impartial games.

IAFahim.Geometry.Advanced.readme:
# IAFahim.Geometry.Advanced

## Use case
Curious cat uses advanced geometry when plain lines and circles are not enough. It tackles robust intersections, hulls, and tricky predicates.
